title: An interpolated 2022 Gaia20cdd depth test permits ice screens and gives a strong model 3.1 um band
abstract: We test whether foreground structure can remove the failure of pure-ice dust models for the 2022 Gaia20cdd dip. We integrate extinction through the measured band responses and use positive column mixtures. No clump shape or covering fraction is fixed. We test 936 grain cases; 61 pass a published slow-colour rule. For the published five-band depth vector, all 15 selected broad ice populations fail three-error boxes. A conservative bound for every column gives W1 attenuation of at least 0.634 mag, against 0.412 +/- 0.034 mag. The input bands sample a changing three-day event. An interpolation of corrected g and r flux to 43 infrared times gives depths 3.430 and 3.198 mag. With a 0.10 mag optical allowance and the lone i datum omitted, some broad ice models pass: their smallest common error multiplier is 2.288, compared with 5.436 for the published vector. In this sensitivity case, all six feasible tested ice populations give a photosphere-divided model 3.1 um feature depth of 0.805-0.913. Feasible silicate and graphite models give -0.0284 to +0.0002. Fractional linear programs and monotonic dual bounds cover every positive column distribution for each tested grain population. Independent Mie checks, grid refinements, witnesses, certificates, source hashes and retrieval code are supplied. These are conditional model results, not an ice detection or confidence interval. Non-simultaneous bands, interpolation, median infrared summaries, nominal 266 K ice constants, common source weights, a finite grain family and fixed emission limit the result.

display.caption: The compatibility of ice screens depends on how the changing event is summarized. With the published optical vector, broad ice populations require more W1 dimming than measured even for arbitrary foreground columns. Separate error boxes are not joint confidence regions.

At the interpolated 2022 state, the tested feasible pure-ice screens require a strong photosphere-divided model 3.1 um feature. Tested silicate and graphite screens give a nearly smooth diagnostic. The bounds include every column distribution for each fixed tested grain population. They assume the stated spectra, source weights and emission correction.
